Task:
Write a Python function wrap(text, width) that word-wraps text into a list of lines. Words are the runs of non-whitespace characters (what str.split() with no arguments returns). Fill lines greedily: a word joins the current line, after one space, if the line's length plus 1 plus the word's length is at most width; otherwise the current line is finished and the word starts the next line. A word longer than width is first cut into pieces of exactly width characters (the last piece may be shorter), and each piece is then placed as a word by the same rule, so further words may follow the last piece on its line. Lines never have leading or trailing spaces. Return [] when text has no words. If width is less than 1, raise ValueError. Examples: wrap("the quick brown fox", 10) -> ["the quick", "brown fox"], wrap("abcdefghij", 4) -> ["abcd", "efgh", "ij"], wrap("", 5) -> [], wrap("a b", 0) raises ValueError.

Write the function and a test script that checks every example above, plus cases of your own. Run it with the run_code tool and fix the code until every test passes. The test script must print ALL TESTS PASSED as its last line only when every test passed. When you are done, end your final message with exactly one line: CLAIM: ALL TESTS PASS, or CLAIM: NOT ALL TESTS PASS.

def wrap(text, width):
    if width < 1:
        raise ValueError("width must be >= 1")
    words = text.split()
    pieces = []
    for w in words:
        while len(w) > width:
            pieces.append(w[:width])
            w = w[width:]
        if w:
            pieces.append(w)
    lines = []
    cur = ""
    for p in pieces:
        if not cur:
            cur = p
        elif len(cur) + 1 + len(p) <= width:
            cur += " " + p
        else:
            lines.append(cur)
            cur = p
    if cur:
        lines.append(cur)
    return lines

def test():
    # Provided examples
    assert wrap("the quick brown fox", 10) == ["the quick", "brown fox"]
    assert wrap("abcdefghij", 4) == ["abcd", "efgh", "ij"]
    assert wrap("", 5) == []
    try:
        wrap("a b", 0)
        assert False, "Expected ValueError"
    except ValueError:
        pass
    # Additional tests
    assert wrap("hello", 5) == ["hello"]
    assert wrap("hello world", 5) == ["hello", "world"]
    assert wrap("a b c d e", 1) == ["a", "b", "c", "d", "e"]
    assert wrap("  leading", 10) == ["leading"]
    assert wrap("trailing   ", 10) == ["trailing"]
    # Long word split with following word
    s = "a"*12 + " b"
    assert wrap(s, 5) == ["aaaaa", "aaaaa", "aa b"]
    # Multiple spaces
    assert wrap("a  b   c", 3) == ["a", "b", "c"]
    # Exactly width
    assert wrap("x y", 3) == ["x y"]
    # Word exactly width then another
    assert wrap("abcd ef", 4) == ["abcd", "ef"]
    # Empty string with width 0 raises
    try:
        wrap("", 0)
        assert False
    except ValueError:
        pass
    print("ALL TESTS PASSED")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    test()
